parts.note: slush is mawkish, silly sentimental writing or talk
a fund is a sum of money set aside

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a pot of cash as soppy, sentimental money.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: SLUSH (soppy sentiment) plus FUND (money) builds the phrase, and the clue as a whole loosely describes money of a dubious kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A slush fund is a reserve of cash kept for bribes or other improper payments, so it is money of a disreputable sort.

parts.note: a Lett is a native of Latvia
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A woman owned a set of jewels from Latvia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' is only a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old English woman's given name, so it names a particular lady.

indicators.note: mentioned means the word is spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a surplice is a loose white vestment worn by clergy and choristers

explanation.surface: Someone talks about a spare piece of church clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left over beyond what is needed is an excess, an extra amount.

clue.text: Not able to see why one cannot take off

definitions.text: Not able to see why one cannot take off

parts.words: Not able to see why one cannot take off
parts.note: reads like puzzlement over a stalled plan, but describes a plane or airport stuck because thick mist has cut visibility

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled about why they are not allowed to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not able to see why' sounds like bewilderment; in fact the plane literally cannot see, which is why it is grounded.
explanation.definitionFit: When thick mist stops flights, an airport or aircraft is kept on the ground by poor visibility.

clue.text: Wasted away, we hear, over a number of years

indicators.note: we hear tells us to take a word that sounds like the one defined

parts.note: decayed means rotted or wasted away

explanation.surface: Something gradually crumbled away over a long span of years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link word. In many accents the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A span of ten years is a specific number of years.

parts.note: describes a stock British stereotype of a brash young woman, and also literally any girl from Harlow, a town in that county

explanation.surface: A caricature of an unrefined woman who lives in Harlow.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlow is a new town in the county north-east of London; the stereotype of a loud, showy young woman is named after that county, so the question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A British stereotype of a brash, fashion-obsessed, unsophisticated young woman, named after a county near London that contains Harlow.

clue.text: Many trails in a whirl as result of strong wind

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

indicators.note: spinning in a whirl, the letters of trails are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Lots of paths swirling about as a result of a strong gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as result of' is linking; 'in a whirl' rearranges TRAILS into ISTRAL, which follows M.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a cold northerly wind that blows down the Rhône valley into southern France.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the present is the time now

explanation.surface: An instruction to take action on something without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To act for someone is to stand in for them as their delegate.

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a suite is a matching set, as of furniture or rooms

explanation.surface: A hotel advert describing a bathroom within a French apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A washroom opening directly off a bedroom is described with this French phrase.

clue.text: Safekeeping at home or in the theatre

indicators.note: the word or is at home, settled, inside the next piece
in places the word or within the theatre piece

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession

explanation.surface: Asking whether valuables are best kept safe at home or in a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at home' and 'in' together say that OR lives inside STAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping goods stored away somewhere secure is a form of safe custody.

clue.text: One reformed one who helps in a crime

definitions.text: one who helps in a crime

parts.note: a means one
someone reformed has been made better

explanation.surface: A former criminal who has gone straight, now assisting a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice who encourages or assists wrongdoing is said to abet it.

parts.note: Bill is a short form of William

indicators.note: accepted means the playwright's nickname takes the ring inside it

parts.note: the Bard is the usual nickname for Shakespeare
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: William Shakespeare took on a ring in a theatrical scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'William Shakespeare' to be one person; it splits into two pieces. 'Hoarding' is British for a big outdoor advertising board.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a hoarding is a large outdoor panel for posters.

parts.note: a regime is a government or administration

explanation.surface: A government had a fresh policy on food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' is linking. 'diet' looks like a parliament but is the eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed course of food and exercise for health is a dietary programme.

clue.text: Swimmer on the green found flowering plant in the water

parts.note: an eel is a fish, a swimmer
a village green is an area of grass

explanation.surface: A fish lying on a lawn found a water plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'found' are linking; the first piece sits on the second in the down sense of the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a seagrass, a marine flowering plant that grows submerged in shallow coastal waters.

definitions.meaning: to let something mature, as timber or wine
a quarter of the year, such as spring or winter

explanation.surface: Ripening over a quarter of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoning lets timber or food mature, and spring, summer, autumn and winter each last about three months.

clue.text: Clever comical person has means of payment

parts.note: smart means clever
a card is a joker, an amusing person

explanation.surface: A witty, funny person has a way of paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastic chip-bearing card used to pay electronically is a payment method.

indicators.note: mucky suggests something messed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone hoses down a dirty building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mucky' rearranges HOSES OUT A.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln for drying hops, typical of Kent, is a farm structure with a cowled roof.

indicators.note: original suggests making something new, so the letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A wedded person's first sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' rearranges MARRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adores another person is a fan or suitor.

indicators.note: in puts the word for behold inside the rearranged letters
different signals that places is put into another order

parts.note: lo is an old word for behold, look

explanation.surface: Look at shellfish found in various places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges PLACES into ESCALP, and 'in' puts LO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant name for the scallop, a bivalve mollusc.

clue.text: Posh girl first having speed to move about joyfully

indicators.note: first means the girl comes ahead of the posh letter

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
U means upper-class, posh
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A posh young woman is the first to rush around happily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh girl' reads as one phrase, but 'first' puts GAL before U. U means upper-class in British usage. 'having' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound or prance clumsily and exuberantly, a word coined by Lewis Carroll.

explanation.surface: A minor brush-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minor is of little weight, and a pointed rebuff is an insult.

indicators.note: potential hints at what something could become, so these letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Possible income is visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' rearranges EARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something within reach of sight or a weapon is close enough to be seen.

parts.note: suggests a woman performer on stage, but means a woman who receives and looks after guests

explanation.surface: A woman who performs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertainer' suggests a performer; here it is a woman who entertains guests at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who welcomes and looks after guests at a party is the person giving it.

parts.note: real means genuine
a period is a span of time

explanation.surface: Actual time spent working at a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: in computing the phrase means processing done instantly, as events actually happen.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing it describes processing that keeps pace with actual events, with no delay.

clue.text: Crowded round bomb defused by Edward

indicators.note: defused suggests the bomb is taken apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward made a bomb safe and people gathered round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like part of the wordplay but belongs to the definition; 'defused' gives MOBB, and 'by' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity surrounded by a throng of fans has been swarmed.

definitions.meaning: a person who takes others over the water, a single person going over
the opening across clue in a crossword

explanation.surface: The boatman deserves the opening crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on 'Ferryman': a person who carries passengers over water is literally a single person going over, which the phrase also says.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is a person who crosses, a ferryman; in a crossword it labels the first horizontal clue.

clue.text: Pass round fashionable mob converting electric charge

indicators.note: round means the pass goes around the fashionable letter

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
U means upper-class, hence smart or fashionable

indicators.note: converting means the letters of mob are changed into another order

explanation.surface: A mountain pass surrounded by a trendy crowd that is changing electrical charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like a verb but is the mountain col. U for upper-class, hence fashionable, is a crossword convention; 'converting' gives OMB.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the SI unit of electric charge, the amount carried by one ampere in one second.

indicators.note: accepted means the short name takes the drooping word inside

parts.note: Bet is a short form of Elizabeth
lank hair hangs limp and drooping

explanation.surface: Elizabeth took a sagging bedcover.
explanation.definitionFit: A large woollen sheet laid over a bed is a covering.

clue.text: Exam did not start before the heartless retort

indicators.note: before puts the shortened exam ahead of the next piece
did not start means the first letter of the exam is dropped

parts.note: the Tripos is the final honours exam at Cambridge University

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An exam that never began prompted a cruel comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tripos is Cambridge University's honours exam; without its first letter it gives RIPOS. 'heartless' strips the middle of THE to leave TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick, sharp reply is a witty comeback.

clue.text: Upset with illness going round small place

indicators.note: going round means the illness surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: disease means illness
PL is the short form of place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at sickness spreading around a little village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is linking; 'small' tells us to abbreviate place.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to annoy or offend them.
